dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "All 17 flagged annual renewals have valid dealer IDs (8 for DLR-104 and 9 for DLR-219), unique `recharge_id` and `source_event_id` values, and effective dates from May 1–28 while being posted on May 31."
"Dealer cash equals ledger with $0 reconciliation difference"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The May 31 West annual-plan cluster is supported by the recharge-level data as a legitimate month-end posting batch."
"The effective dates precede the May 31 posting date, the amounts reconcile exactly to cash and ledger, and the month-end posting convention is described as contractually permitted."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The main remaining unknown is whether any downstream system recognized the same 17 source events more than once outside the supplied recharge extract."
"Evidence of a second financial recognition, duplicate entitlement posting, or another ledger entry for the same source events would change the decision to an escalation for duplicate revenue."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "perform a read-only downstream check that the 17 source events have only one financial/entitlement recognition."
"Do not reverse or alter the May 31 revenue."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Separately raise a data-quality ticket for the 16,260 missing `dealer_id` records"
"with no changes to the flagged revenue unless the downstream check identifies duplicate recognition."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No material issue / no escalation for duplicate revenue or manipulated reporting" is well supported for the supplied extract, but the external entitlement check remains unperformed.
"No economic duplicate was identified" is stronger than the demonstrated tests: unique `recharge_id` and `source_event_id` values do not by themselves exclude all economic duplication.

"Pipeline defect causing the May 31 cluster — rejected" is somewhat overstated because completeness, identifier uniqueness, and reconciliation do not rule out every possible pipeline defect; they mainly weaken the duplicate-processing explanation.

"supported by the recharge-level data as a legitimate month-end posting batch" appropriately identifies timing, but legitimacy is corroborated rather than conclusively established by the email and supplied reconciliation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A downstream duplicate financial or entitlement recognition could still exist outside the supplied recharge extract, despite unique recharge and source-event IDs and zero cash-to-ledger difference. The submission explicitly preserves this possibility and proposes checking it. A broader pipeline defect remains a secondary alternative, particularly given the missing-dealer-ID population, but the submission reasonably distinguishes it from the flagged records.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Actually perform and document the proposed read-only join/check of the 17 `source_event_id` values against downstream financial and entitlement records, including the query, matched row counts, and reconciliation results, rather than leaving duplicate entitlement recognition as an unresolved unknown.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South region support ticket volume fell following the NovaIVR pilot rollout."
"Technical service events (outages/escalations) surged concurrently in the South region."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Callers interacting with NovaIVR experience high rates of repeat calls within 7 days."

"Resolution markers in interaction logs show that callers frequently bounce back to human agents or log parallel complaints via alternative channels (email/tickets) shortly after interacting with the IVR."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "True Customer Intent: Whether callers abandoned the IVR out of satisfaction or out of frustration with the menu structure (frustration-driven abandonment)."

"Hypothesis: The ticket drop reflects a seasonal dip in regional service issues.\n\nWhy rejected: Historical comparison against other regions and service event logs show that underlying technical faults actually increased during the pilot window."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "there is no sufficient evidence to claim that, the South-region complaint drop proves NovaIVR success and justifies national expansion."
"Pause regional expansion and implement a 14-day post-IVR customer sentiment survey coupled with closed-loop tracking to measure first-contact resolution (FCR) accurately."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Person to Question: Farah Iqbal (Customer Care Operations)"
"How do we currently track customers who abandon the NovaIVR system—do we see an increase in immediate redial rates or transfers to escalation queues?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The claim that callers experience "high rates" of repeat calls is not quantified or tied to specific cohorts, fields, or comparison rates.
The claim that technical service events "surged concurrently" is not supported with dates, counts, regional comparison, or a reproducible query.

The statement that "Resolution markers in interaction logs show that callers frequently bounce back to human agents or log parallel complaints via alternative channels (email/tickets)" has no direct source citation or defined resolution-marker logic.
The claim that the pilot was deployed "without clear CX metrics" may be supported by the email, but the submission does not quote the relevant passage or identify the excluded metrics.
The proposed 14-day sentiment survey is presented without evidence that it will capture customers whose cases were never created, repeat contacts, or actual journey resolution.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately considers seasonal variation and the possibility that abandonment reflects either satisfaction or frustration rather than treating abandonment as proof of dissatisfaction. However, it misses the strongest measurement-process explanation: NovaIVR failures may prevent case creation, making the ticket decline an observation failure rather than a real reduction in customer friction. It also does not clearly distinguish technical service events from complaints or establish that those events should move one-for-one.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible end-to-end analysis linking IVR sessions to case creation, transfers, repeat contacts, and subsequent outcomes, including pre/post South cohorts and comparison regions; then validate the linkage with sampled call listening before making any expansion decision.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv` for “impact_mw = 0” and “cleared = yes,” which supports those two claims if the fields are as stated.
The claim that there are “only four low-severity or informational entries over a multi-week span” is not tied to specific rows, timestamps, severity fields, or event text.
“Quick resolution” is asserted in the finding but no duration field or timestamps are cited.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission makes a basic cross-check between zero generation impact and `cleared = yes`.

Its rejection of “critical equipment failures” relies only on impact and clearance status; it does not test whether the wording reflects a communications warning, whether event labels are mixed, or whether clearance could occur without a production impact.
No independent channel or plausible innocent alternative is examined beyond the binary failure/loss hypothesis.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The table assigns “High” confidence to the two cited field-level claims, appropriately reflecting direct log fields.

The conclusion “nothing in the export warrants escalation or further time investment” is broader than the evidence and does not state what remains unknown, such as the meaning of mixed event wording or whether the export is complete.
The submission does not identify the smallest decision-changing check.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Stop” is broadly sensible given the stated zero-MW impact and cleared statuses.

The absolute recommendation to invest no further time omits a proportionate low-priority quality check of inconsistent or mixed event wording, if present, and proposes no discriminating follow-up test.
The action is therefore directionally appropriate but somewhat over-scoped.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion not to escalate is directionally supported by the submission's cited `impact_mw = 0` and `cleared = yes` observations.

The wording “nothing ... warrants escalation or further time investment” overstates what those fields establish: they support no apparent production loss or unresolved event, not necessarily the absence of any data-quality or communications issue.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The dataset contains only four low-severity or informational entries” is unsupported by the cited evidence table, which does not identify row count, severity, or event classification fields.
“Over a multi-week span” and “quick resolution” are not supported with cited timestamps or durations.

“The evidence rejects” critical equipment failures is too strong: zero MW impact and clearance reject an observed generation-loss consequence, but do not by themselves establish that no equipment issue occurred.
“Nothing ... warrants escalation or further time investment” is overbroad because a low-priority wording or data-quality check could still be reasonable.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: These may be routine communications or informational warnings with no operational consequence, rather than equipment failures; the mixed wording, if present, is best treated as a low-priority export-quality check rather than a reason to escalate.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Trace each event row's timestamp, severity/status wording, and any duration or recovery fields, and perform one independent cross-check of the zero-MW impact before stopping; this would distinguish a routine communications warning from a merely cleared event without searching for an unsupported failure narrative.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md` for Rs 662,444, Rs 453,086, and the 31.6% arithmetic.
It cites `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf` for banded deviation charges and rates.
It does not cite or use the relevant 29 May `base_schedule_mw` and `submitted_schedule_mw` fields, which provide a same-day comparison.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly states that “n=1 per method entirely confounds the AI intervention with day-to-day weather variability.”
It identifies plausible alternatives including forecast error, block-level wind variance, and operator intervention.
However, it treats the evidence as only two single-day methods and does not test the available same-day base-versus-submitted schedule comparison on 29 May.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission appropriately says the 31.6% figure is “statistically invalid as causal proof.”
It narrows the claim to the workflow being feasible and correlated with lower generation gaps and penalty exposure.
It does not quantify or acknowledge the smaller same-day benefit, so its uncertainty is well calibrated for the headline claim but incomplete for the pilot's observed performance.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to retain the workbook in O&M while prohibiting automated settlement or unverified reliance is proportionate to the causal uncertainty.
The proposed shadow-mode or retrospective validation addresses day-to-day weather confounding.
The next test is not maximally discriminating because it omits the immediate same-day counterfactual analysis and gives an unsupported specificity to “n >= 30 events.”

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly distinguishes a mathematically accurate 31.6% comparison from causal proof.
It preserves some value by describing lower observed generation gaps and penalty exposure rather than concluding that the pilot had no value.
It misses the required qualification that 29 May's base-versus-submitted schedules show a smaller same-day improvement, so it is somewhat under-scoped.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “A sample size of n=1 per method” overlooks the available within-day 29 May comparison between `base_schedule_mw` and `submitted_schedule_mw`.

“The narrower claim supported by the evidence is ... correlated with a narrower generation gap” is incomplete because the same-day schedule fields support a more informative, though still non-causal, within-day comparison.
The assertion that identical wind profiles, turbulence, and cut-out timing were not verified is plausible but is not tied to specific supplied fields or measurements.
The recommendation's requirement for “all recurrences ... over the next quarter” is operationally plausible but not justified by a stated decision threshold or power calculation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% reduction between 28 and 29 May is not a controlled causal estimate because the days differ. Nevertheless, on 29 May the submitted schedule can be compared with the base schedule within the same weather day, showing a smaller but meaningful observed improvement. The evidence therefore supports retaining the pilot as promising and operationally useful, while withholding attribution of the full 31.6% reduction to AI until matched-event validation is completed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Calculate and report the 29 May same-day counterfactual using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw`, including the resulting generation-gap and penalty differences, then use matched high-wind events to test whether that within-day benefit repeats.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the declaration claim to `declaration.pdf`: "Product P1001 is declared under tariff code 90211000 on the Swiss customs declaration."
It ties the local-code claim to `country_tariff_matrix.xlsx`: "The approved Swiss local tariff code for P1001 in the country matrix is 90211000."
It ties the mismatch to `product_master_current.xlsx`: "The global Helios master commodity code for P1001 is 90211090."
The submission acknowledges a limitation: "Direct confirmation output from the official Swiss Tares online tariff database for the specific import date" is missing.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: It explicitly tests and rejects one alternative: "Hypothesis: The broker committed a transposition error by declaring 90211000 instead of the master code 90211090."

Its explanation identifies the jurisdictional mechanism: "Switzerland uses a distinct national tariff nomenclature where P1001 maps explicitly to 90211000 per local trade operations guidance, not the standard 8-digit Helios export code."
The analysis does not test whether the country matrix is current, whether the product classification itself is correct, or whether the declaration date and applicable tariff version align.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The evidence table labels the three core file-based claims "High" confidence.
It appropriately identifies missing date-specific official corroboration: "Direct confirmation output from the official Swiss Tares online tariff database for the specific import date" is absent.
However, the conclusion states the code is "correct and compliant" and the alert was a "false positive" despite acknowledging that the official date-specific tariff confirmation is missing.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the data-lineage mismatch between "the declared Swiss tariff code (90211000)" and "the global Helios master code (90211090)."
It identifies the system behavior as "a cross-jurisdictional comparison against the global Helios master code."

It proposes the corresponding control change: "update the validation rule engine to accommodate Swiss national tariff codes instead of enforcing global Helios master codes uniformly across all jurisdictions."
It gives limited treatment to governance, versioning, effective dates, or how the local matrix is maintained and validated.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommended disposition is proportionate to the identified mismatch: "Do not escalate the code mismatch as a declaration error."
The proposed remediation addresses recurrence: "update the validation rule engine to accommodate Swiss national tariff codes."

The action "Close the automated exception alert as a false positive" is somewhat premature without first documenting the import date, confirming the applicable Swiss tariff version, and testing the rule change; the submission does not specify those safeguards.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The declared Swiss tariff code (90211000) is correct and compliant" is stronger than the cited internal records establish because the submission itself lacks official Swiss Tares confirmation for the specific import date.

"The automated flag was a false positive" is plausible and consistent with the cited code mismatch, but the submission does not provide the alert logic or evidence that the rule actually compared the Swiss declaration with the global master code.

"Switzerland uses a distinct national tariff nomenclature ... per local trade operations guidance" cites no separate guidance file; the evidence table cites only the country tariff matrix for the local mapping.
"Close the automated exception alert" is not adequately conditioned on date-specific validation and documentation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The country tariff matrix or product mapping could be stale, misclassified, or inapplicable to the declaration date, so 90211000 might still be erroneous despite the apparent jurisdictional mismatch; this alternative is less supported than the benign Swiss-versus-global-code explanation but was not directly tested.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the applicable Swiss Tares tariff code and effective date for P1001, then document the alert rule's compared fields and implement the jurisdiction-aware rule only after controlled testing and approval.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability (evidence)
citations: The submission identifies specific records and references, including "Customs Declaration IE-2025-000411 & Commercial Invoice INV-000411," "review_note.txt," "packet_manifest.txt," and `supplier_origin_register.csv`.
It precisely identifies the declarations `SD-SUP-01-P1006-2025` and `SD-SUP-02-P1006-2024`, including the latter's expiry date of "2025-07-31."
A limitation is acknowledged through the missing evidence: "The actual document file or audit trail for supplier declaration reference `SD-SUP-01-P1006-2025` attached to the ClearView packet."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing (reasoning)
citations: The response explicitly tests two hypotheses: "The shipment qualifies for preference under an Irish supplier route (SUP-02)" and "No valid supplier declaration exists for this product and period."
It correctly distinguishes a system-linking issue from total absence by stating, "The review flag only indicates a lack of *linking* in ClearView, not the total absence of a source document."

However, the rejection of the Irish route partly relies on "all commercial shipping documents consistently state the manufacturing country is the United States," which does not by itself resolve preferential-origin rules or exclude another valid qualification route.

dimensions.name: Calibration (calibration)
citations: The conclusion is qualified as "unsupported in ClearView" rather than declaring fraud or invalidity, and it identifies the active declaration as existing while noting that it is not linked.

The submission lists specific uncertainty: "Explicit mapping confirmation linking shipper \"Asterion Manufacturing Services\" to supplier ID SUP-01" and "The specific trade agreement rules-engine logic used by broker BRK-D."

The phrase "valid active US supplier declaration" is somewhat stronger than the evidence described, because the actual declaration document and its preferential-origin content were not verified in the packet.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding (systems)
citations: The response recognizes a data-lineage problem by contrasting "unlinked supplier documentation" with an active register entry and by recommending that the reference be "formally link[ed]" in ClearView.
It identifies relevant actors and systems—"ClearView," "broker BRK-D," and the "Supplier Origin Register."

It does not sufficiently explain whether the register is authoritative, how supplier IDs map to the shipper, how the system determines eligibility, or how manufacturing-country data differs from preferential-origin qualification.

dimensions.name: Decision safety (action)
citations: The proposed action is proportionate: "Pause final clearance approval on the preference claim" rather than alleging fraud or stopping all shipment activity.
It proposes a reversible verification step: "formally link valid US supplier declaration reference `SD-SUP-01-P1006-2025` (SUP-01) within ClearView."

The action should also require verification of the declaration's actual contents and applicable agreement rules, not merely linking the reference, because the submission itself says the "specific trade agreement rules-engine logic" is missing.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Goods originate in the United States and claim preference (0.0% duty)" is supported as a documentary statement, but the submission does not establish that United States manufacturing country equals preferential origin or that the agreement's qualification rules are met.

Calling `SD-SUP-01-P1006-2025` a "valid active US supplier declaration" is supported by the register entry as described, but its actual document, authenticity, supplier mapping, and substantive preferential-origin terms remain unverified.

The statement that an Irish supplier route is rejected because documents state United States manufacturing country overstates what commercial documents can establish; they do not alone exclude alternative preferential-origin routes or demonstrate the relevant origin rule.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may be substantively valid, and the apparent defect may be only a ClearView linkage or data-lineage failure, if `SD-SUP-01-P1006-2025` is authentic, maps Asterion Manufacturing Services to SUP-01, covers P1006 and the declaration date, and satisfies the applicable trade-agreement rule. Conversely, the register entry may be insufficient if it records administrative validity without the underlying supplier evidence or required origin content.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify and document the underlying `SD-SUP-01-P1006-2025`, its mapping to the shipper and product, and the applicable preferential-origin rule before treating the active register status as sufficient support; explicitly separate manufacturing country from preferential origin.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "among 220 records with a QCore timestamp, median is 39.4 h and mean is 45.5 h" — identifies the file and fields supporting the observed cycle-time statistic.
"The SOP says routine service is ‘24 hours from required evidence available to disposition.’" — quotes the governing definition.
"185/220 (84%) of populated timestamps are exactly 02:10:00" and "source_freshness.csv: LabTrack, CertVault" — triangulates timestamp-pattern and freshness evidence while acknowledging limitations.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Receipt-to-release therefore includes time that the SOP does not necessarily measure" — separates the observed symptom from the defined service-time mechanism.
"This could be genuine standardized processing, but it could also indicate an ETL/batch timestamp" — preserves competing explanations.

The proposed sample verifies both the semantic meaning of qcore_release_ts and the point at which all required prerequisites were available, providing discriminating tests rather than assuming causality.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "not established" and "unusual enough to verify" — appropriately avoids treating qcore_release_ts as definitively an authorization event.
"42 of 262 records have disposition=HOLD and no qcore_release_ts" — bounds selection bias in the observed population.
"If those timestamps cannot be supplied reliably, the appropriate KPI is ‘insufficient evidence to measure SOP cycle time’" — makes the recommendation conditional on evidence quality.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do Not use One and Half day figure as KPI" — directly reframes the decision around the actual SOP definition.

"Build the dashboard only as a clearly labelled descriptive receipt-to-QCore-disposition metric for now, not as a Quality service-level/performance KPI" — provides a safe, reversible interim action that avoids operationalizing a potentially misleading KPI.
The recommendation protects against optimizing an interface or batch-timestamp artifact while preserving useful descriptive reporting.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly tests and rejects using the SOP target, lab_complete_ts, filtering obvious exceptions, and assuming qcore_release_ts is the disposition event.
"Even a proxy subset ... still has a median ... about 35.0 h" — uses a filtered alternative analysis rather than merely listing exceptions.
"This could be genuine standardized processing, but it could also indicate an ETL/batch timestamp" — states what competing interpretation remains viable and how to test it.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "take a small sample ... 10–20 across sites and with both 02:10:00 and non-02:10:00 QCore timestamps" — specifies a focused, high-value sample.

The two requested checks ask for the exact qcore_release_ts event and the earliest time all SOP prerequisites were available; these directly discriminate measurement artifact from real workflow delay.
The proposed evidence would change whether the metric can be used as an SOP KPI, making the request decision-linked rather than generic.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that a 10–20 record sample is the “smallest” decision-changing verification is a reasonable operational proposal, but it is not demonstrated statistically and may not establish timestamp semantics across all systems or sites.
The submission identifies uneven source freshness but could more explicitly test whether QCore and LabTrack records are from a coherent common as-of snapshot before joining them.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10:00 concentration could reflect a genuine standardized authorization or scheduled release process rather than an ETL artifact, and the long receipt-to-release interval could include legitimate pre-evidence waiting time. The submission correctly leaves this open pending event-level timestamp verification.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly reconcile source snapshots and event semantics in the sample: obtain QCore, LabTrack, certificate, and deviation-resolution records with their as-of/extract timestamps and compare the event log timestamps for the same batches before calculating any end-to-end KPI.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "spare_parts.csv (rows 0, 1, 2)"; "part_restrictions.csv"; "source_freshness.csv" — Key claims are tied to relevant files, fields, and some row references, and the submission triangulates inventory, restrictions, policy, email, and freshness evidence. It does not consistently provide exact row-level support for every candidate or quote the precise policy clauses.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "the bottleneck is operational and governance-related, not merely descriptive"; "Global available quantities can lag behind local reservations" — The submission separates semantic retrieval from transferability and identifies revision, reservation, qualification, and freshness mechanisms. It could better distinguish whether each candidate fails because of policy, technical incompatibility, or simply missing confirmation.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Needs Engineering Check"; "global available quantity may lag local reservations"; "The decision to classify $0 ... as immediately actionable" — Candidate-level uncertainty is generally explicit and availability freshness is recognized. However, "$0" is presented more definitively than the evidence supports, and "over a month stale" may not be accurate for all July request dates when the snapshot is dated 2026-06-26.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not automate cross-site purchase cancellations or transfers based solely on current global catalog search hits"; "Actionability Status & Reason" — This is a useful safety-oriented reframing and distinguishes candidate matches from actionable transfers. The recommendation lacks a small reversible pilot, explicit success criteria, and a prioritized workflow for validating the four candidates.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "High semantic similarity and matching manufacturer part numbers mean purchase requests can be automatically intercepted and canceled"; "The apparent total external quote value ... represents immediate savings" — Two plausible but unsafe interpretations are rejected using reservation, revision, logistics, qualification, and freshness evidence. The analysis does not fully test other competing explanations such as procurement lead-time requirements, duplicate demand, or erroneous source records.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "What Would change the decision"; "Real-time, Synchronized Inventory Visibility"; "Formal engineering approval"; "Written clearance" — The submission requests relevant evidence and identifies decision gates, but it gives four broad conditions rather than prioritizing the smallest, highest-value query, responsible owner, or specific test that would discriminate among the candidate failure modes.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Leadership’s suspicion ... is correct" is stronger than the presented evidence establishes; the examples show description variation and candidate matches, but not that this is the primary cause of plant purchasing.

"Not Transferable" for the Rev A/Rev B servo case is too definitive without an engineering interchangeability determination; the evidence establishes that it is not currently actionable without review, not necessarily permanently nontransferable.

"Replacing batch-lagged ... snapshots with live local CMMS availability would eliminate 'ghost stock' risks" overstates the effect of freshness improvement, since reservations, qualification, revision, and UOM constraints would still require confirmation.
The claim that the MaintStar snapshot is "over a month stale" is not uniformly supported for requests dated shortly after 2026-06-26.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The evidence may support semantic search as a useful candidate-generation tool while showing that the current four examples are not yet transfer-ready; it does not necessarily establish that governance is the dominant enterprise bottleneck or that none of the candidates can be transferred after routine local confirmation. Some apparent failures could reflect incomplete or asynchronous extracts rather than true operational restrictions.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a prioritized, reversible validation pilot on the highest-value non-revision-mismatch candidate, likely PR-260721 or PR-260711: obtain a current holding-site reservation/availability confirmation and receiving-site qualification decision, record the exact restriction and engineering disposition, and define success as a confirmed transferable quantity and lead time. This would directly separate stale-data, reservation, qualification, and technical-equivalence failure modes before any cancellation or transfer automation.
